Action Plan:
1. Arrange urgent same-day clinic visit for physical review, hydration assessment, and stool specimen collection for microbiology.  
2. Advise continuation of oral rehydration solution (ORS) in frequent small sips; monitor urine output (aim ≥ 4 voids/day, light yellow).  
3. Dietary advice: bland foods (toast, plain biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, dairy, fatty or spicy meals until recovery.  
4. Provide clear safety-net: attend Emergency Department if unable to keep any fluids down, passing little/no urine, dizziness, worsening abdominal pain, sustained high fever, or blood in stool.  
5. Appointment booking to be completed via Babylon support line; patient to telephone if symptoms progress before scheduled review.  
6. No empiric antibiotics prescribed; await stool culture results to guide therapy.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for call: 3-day history of severe diarrhoea and vomiting.  
• History of presenting illness  
  – Onset: 3 days ago; began watery, now very loose stools; ≥ 4 bowel motions today (“lost count”).  
  – Vomiting: persistent; last episode ~2 h before call; “cannot keep anything down,” including water and ORS.  
  – Fever: subjective “boiling,” no thermometer reading.  
  – Abdominal pain: colicky, centred at umbilicus; worsens before urge to defecate.  
  – No blood in stool or urine; no rash.  
  – Urination: last void 1 h ago; colour not noted.  
  – Possible exposure: brother with identical illness; school outbreak reported; no recent travel.  
• Past medical / surgical history: none significant; no prior gastrointestinal disease or surgery.  
• Medications: vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional ibuprofen for dysmenorrhoea; ORS sachet (salt-sugar mix) taken 3 ×/day for 2 days.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Gynecologic: last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; not sexually active; no contraception.  
• Social: Non-smoker; occasional alcohol; works as graphic designer; living with mother and brother.  
• Family: brother currently symptomatic with similar illness.

Objective:
(Remote consultation – limited examination)  
• General: Appears unwell on video, reporting subjective fever.  
• Abdomen: Reports marked tenderness around umbilicus on self-palpation.  
• Hydration: Able to pass urine 1 h prior to call; no objective signs assessed.  
• Vitals: Not measured.  
Investigations to date: None.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute diarrhoea and vomiting (gastroenteritis):
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus) – DDx item “Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus)” (High).  
   – Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute bacterial gastroenteritis / food-borne infection – DDx (Medium); stool culture ordered.  
     • Food-borne toxin–mediated illness – DDx (Low–Medium); less likely given 72 h duration.  
     • Inflammatory bowel disease flare – DDx (Low); no chronic history.  
   – Investigations planned: Stool culture; in-clinic assessment of hydration status (vital signs, basic bloods if indicated).  
   – Treatment planned: Continue ORS with small frequent sips; simple diet as above; no antibiotics unless bacterial pathogen confirmed.  
   – Relevant referrals: None at present; urgent clinic appointment arranged, with escalation to Emergency Department if deterioration.

2. Risk of dehydration secondary to vomiting/diarrhoea:
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Mild dehydration (clinical risk).  
   – Differential diagnosis: None separate (secondary to Issue 1).  
   – Investigations planned: Clinical assessment of hydration (vital signs, capillary refill, possible serum electrolytes) at urgent visit.  
   – Treatment planned: Ongoing ORS; education on fluid targets; hospital admission if unable to maintain hydration.  
   – Relevant referrals: Emergency Department if meets safety-net criteria.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Allergies not elicited; no objective vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP, weight); medication reconciliation incomplete (vitamin D dose).  
• Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional brief inaudible gaps not affecting clinical content.
